body: Yeah, the bug probably crept in with the same change, but I think this may be a separate issue.

I noticed that `applyExtends()` is called [here](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/1803f87bf4784e5103932e9bcd1e73e595d4e8ef/lib/config.js#L63) with a `filePath` that's an empty string.

But even if that's fixed, in `applyExtends()`, it still takes [a code path](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/11435afd76278a1291566c92af985bf8fad0731f/lib/config/config-file.js#L331) where the `filePath` argument isn't taken into account during `resolve()`.

body:
Did this second case work in ESLint 1.x?

It looks like `eslint-config-standard-jsx` isn't in the lookup path from `eslint`. The call to `require()` is happening inside of `eslint`, so it starts looking up from `eslint/node_modules` and would miss `standard/node_modules` regardless of what I'm doing.

(Side note: It's amazing how much trouble npm 3 introduced with this feature. Just doesn't seem worth it.)

issue.body:
Hello,

it looks like scoped packages do not work correctly on Windows machines. Below you can see that eslint is trying to load a configuration from `@strv\javascript\standard\optional.js/eslint-config`, while the correct place to load it from would be `@strv\eslint-config-javascript\standard\optional.js`.

To provide more context, the file `@strv/javascript/environments/nodejs/optional.js` contains a **relative** reference to another configuration file via `extends` property:

``` js
module.exports = {
  extends: '../../standard/optional.js'
}
```

If it helps, the whole configuration package is publicly available [here](https://github.com/strvcom/js-coding-standards).

I wonder if this is an issue with ESLint or with the configuration package. On OS X, this configuration package works without issues.

Thank you for your help!
